children: U.K. unemployment was unchanged in the three months through July, with the labor market showing continued signs of softness ahead of a Bank of England meeting this week.

The unemployment rate was 4.9%, unchanged from the three months through June, according to data released Tuesday by the Office for National Statistics. This was in line with a consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal.
With the U.K. continuing to face considerable economic uncertainty, employers have preferred to wait and see before committing to further hiring, said Yael Selfin, an economist at KPMG UK.
"People just don't want to hire," she said. "Uncertainty means vacancies are low. They were waiting to see before engaging."
Annual wage growth, excluding bonuses, came in at 3.5%, in line with the prior period and economists' views, the data showed.

The figures come ahead of the Bank of England's interest-rate decision Thursday, with the central bank widely expected to leave its key rate at 3.75%, although markets are increasingly pricing in the possibility of a rate increase later this year as inflation risks have risen.
